articles.title: Broncos hang on to beat the Rams, who blow multiple leads and are a disappointing 1-2 to start this season
articles.summary: The Broncos and Rams played a thriller on Sunday night.
articles.body: Perhaps the Los Angeles Rams will end up being as good as everyone thought this offseason, and their issues early this season will be a fun part of their "America's Game" episode after they win a Super Bowl. But this isn't the start the Rams envisioned. The Rams blew a 16-0 halftime lead and a 26-23 advantage late in the fourth quarter as the Denver Broncos rallied and beat L.A. The Broncos had a clutch drive after giving up the lead on a long pass by Matthew Stafford with 3:38 left. They moved downfield and Bo Nix scored on a jump over the pile for a 1-yard touchdown with 47 seconds left. The Rams rallied and were able to spike the ball with two seconds left at the 14-yard line. After a false start, Stafford threw an interception on the final play of the game and the Broncos held on to a 30-26 win. Hufanga's 2nd INT of the night sealed it 🙌 pic.twitter.com/orLUIr7m2Q— NFL (@NFL) September 28, 2026 The Rams, who played Sunday without injured receiver Puka Nacua and defensive end Myles Garrett, are 1-2 to start the season after being hailed as Super Bowl favorites. The Broncos got some help on their game-winning drive. Rams cornerback Josh Wallace had an interception but a pass interference penalty was called, although it looked on the replay like Wallace didn't commit a foul and Broncos receiver Pat Bryant embellished the contact to draw a flag. The Broncos got another reprieve when an illegal hands to the face penalty kept a drive going after a third-down incompletion. NBC rules analyst Terry McAulay did not believe Rams CB Josh Wallace should have been flagged for pass interference, in what may have otherwise been an interception. The Broncos went on to score what would serve as the game-winning TD. pic.twitter.com/A0YDJ8ZmZl— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) September 28, 2026 The Rams will complain about that phantom call on Wallace, which would have practically sealed the win. But Los Angeles had plenty of chances to put away the game before that. The Broncos hung around until their offense got going, and they pulled out a dramatic win. The Rams were supposed to be above losses like this, or the one they were dealt in the season opener in Australia against the 49ers. It's taking them longer than expected to look like the dominant team everyone expected to see. Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix had a hot second half against the Rams. (AP Photo/Jack Dempsey)AP Photo/Jack DempseyBroncos' start slowDenver's offense was lifeless through the first half. Head coach Sean Payton stressed balance in the offense during a halftime interview, but the run game hadn't been effective enough to sustain drives or for offensive coordinator Davis Webb to call more run plays. Bo Nix wasn't sharp in the passing game against a tough Rams defense, and it led to a first-half shutout. At that point the Broncos had played 10 quarters this season and eight of them on offense had been poor. Denver had a good second half in Week 2 against the Jaguars, and that saved Denver from being 0-2 to start the season. The Broncos finally woke up during their second drive of the third quarter. Nix found Pat Bryant for a touchdown and then had a perfectly placed pass to Jaylen Waddle in the end zone for the 2-point conversion. The Broncos had cut the Rams' lead to 16-8 and for the first time it seemed like there could be a competitive game Sunday night. The Rams had a strong lead in the first half but kept the Broncos in the game. They settled for three field goals in the first half and none were longer than 40 yards. Those missed opportunities were a problem as the Broncos started to gain momentum. Back and forth after halftimeThe Broncos put together another good drive and tied the game. Nix hit Nate Adkins for an 8-yard touchdown and Bryant grabbed the 2-point conversion over a Rams defender to tie the game. The Rams had dominated the first half, and before the third quarter was done their 16-0 lead was gone. The roles had flipped; the Rams suddenly could not move the ball at all. Finally the Rams caught a break. Nix's pass was deflected as it left his hand and Wallace had an easy interception. He returned it to Denver's 37-yard line. A third-down blitz led to a Stafford sack that stalled the drive, but the Rams got a field goal and a 19-16 lead. The Rams batted down a third-and-1 pass after that and the Broncos elected to punt. Davante Adams immediately burned them with a 49-yard gain. It looked at that point like the Rams could start to put the game away. But Stafford threw a pick 6, as he misread the coverage and threw an interception straight to safety Talanoa Hufanga, who returned it 66 yards for a score. The Broncos led 23-19 with 4:49 to go. That was the 33rd pick 6 of Stafford's career, breaking a tie he had for the NFL record with Brett Favre. Stafford has played a lot of football and he wasn't fazed. He hit Konata Mumpfield for three straight completions, gains of 21, 9 and then a 48-yard touchdown to take back the lead. Mumpfield beat cornerback Riley Moss and was wide open downfield for Stafford's pass. The Rams led 26-23. That just meant it was the Broncos' turn to answer. Nix hit Bryant for 39 yards and Troy Franklin for 21, putting Denver in position to at least tie the game with a field goal. Two penalties, including a questionable one on Wallace, kept the drive alive. That led to the Nix touchdown, and the Rams couldn't answer despite getting inside the red zone at the end. The Broncos are happy to be 2-1 after a rough Week 1 loss at Kansas City. The Rams aren't quite as pleased with their start to the season.

articles.title: Sunday featured 12 one-score games, tying the single-week NFL record
articles.summary: With one game to go in Week 3, it has been tied for the most closely contested games in league history.
articles.body:
If Sunday felt like an especially tight set of games in the NFL, your instincts are keen.

Week 3 delivered 12 one-score games in the 15 games (and counting), which is tied for the most in a single week in NFL history, via NBC's Maria Taylor.

The fact that all 12 happened on one day made it feel all the more dramatic and momentous. After a blowout Thursday, with the Falcons stomping the Packers , it was the day the NFL needed — especially with Caleb Williams out and the Bears potentially down to their third-string quarterback when they face the Eagles on Monday night.

The early slate of games Sunday featured seven, maybe even eight decent or better games out of nine. The Steelers and Bengals treated us to an unexpected shootout . The Colts beat the Texans in a rock fight. Now, maybe Giants-Titans wasn't your one-score cup of tea, but there was something around the league for everyone.

Even Chiefs-Dolphins was a one-score game until Kansas City added a cushion touchdown in the final three minutes. The only true stinker was the Jaguars stomping the Patriots , which arguably magnifies the spotlight on New England .

But as the games whittled down, the excitement only grew. The afternoon quartet was 4 for 4: every game within one score, and a few wild ones among them.

Ravens-Cowboys in Brazil was a last-second thriller that had storylines galore: field conditions, two great quarterbacks dueling, huge momentum swings, controversy and a last-second game-winner . Something about the games in that country … all three have been one-score affairs.

Commanders-Seahawks was arguably the most shocking result of Sunday – and maybe the weirdest. Cardinals-49ers never quit on us, either, with the teams trading blows (and points) for four quarters. There wasn't much room to breathe or stretch all afternoon.

The entree, however, arrived Sunday night — the best-for-last thriller between the Rams and Broncos .

When the Rams took a 16-0 halftime lead, it appeared to be headed for Snoozeville. But the Broncos ripped off a 30-10 run to storm back and win , with four lead changes in the fourth quarter. This game also had a serious dose of controversy on a late-game phantom DPI call that crushed the Rams — and probably should have clinched the win for Los Angeles .

Start to finish, Sunday was a monster. It will be hard for Eagles-Bears to upstage Sunday's action, but if the final result is within eight points, we'll have had a record-breaking week in the NFL.

articles.title: Baltimore Ravens produce miracle in Rio de Janeiro, Patrick Mahomes ties Tom Brady and James Cook stars for Buffalo Bills - NFL Sunday review
articles.summary: Welcome to our weekly NFL Sunday Review - Lamar Jackson's Baltimore Ravens produce a miracle finale against the Dallas Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, Brock Purdy stars once again for the undefeated San Francisco 49ers and the Super Bowl champions are beaten
articles.body:
Seven seconds of chaos. Seven seconds to win it all. Seven seconds to send Brazil samba dancing into the night. Seven seconds to crown one of the greatest international games in NFL history. If not the greatest international game in NFL history.

Ricky Martin, baile funk, Lamar Jackson magic, Tyler Loop heroics, Dallas Cowboys disbelief and a last-gasp thriller staged within a cauldron of sporting iconicity. Obrigado, Brazil. Obrigado.

The beach-collared beauty of Rio de Janeiro dazzled on its debut as an NFL host city, its famed magnetism as a hub for otherworldly fun and theatre translating to football as the Baltimore Ravens claimed a 34-31 win over the Dallas Cowboys at the Maracana Stadium.

On a stage graced by Pele and Zico and Romario and Ronaldo and Ronaldinho, it was all too fitting that the very first regular-season game to be played at Rio's sporting home would be decided by a boot. The boot, in this instance, of Tyler Loop.

The Cowboys had just levelled the game at 31-31 on Brandon Aubrey's 23-yard field goal with seven seconds to play, overtime on the horizon as Brazil strapped in for an extended night. Lamar Jackson had other plans, connecting with Zay Flowers for 27 yards to set Baltimore up at the Cowboys 38 on the first play of the ensuing drive. One second left.

Out came Loop, nine months on since he missed the 44-yard field goal that would have gifted the Pittsburgh Steelers the AFC North division title and accompanying playoff berth. Rio redemption would prove sweet as the 25-year-old held his nerve to split the posts from 56 yards and spark a Ravens frenzy.

Loop sprinted off in joyous celebration with a full-speed Jackson and his entire team in tow, spiralling his finger to request some space amid the madness before launching into an imitation of Cristiano Ronaldo's 'SIU', mirrored by the Maracana crowd. Unbridled carnage and the NFL's dream advert for international representation.

The build-up had been marred ever so slightly by question marks over the turf at the Maracana. By the end of Sunday night all had been forgotten as the Ravens showcased their dig deep credentials in the face of a rampant Cowboys offense.

The fourth quarter had depicted the complete Super Bowl contender that Dallas might hope to become this season during a sequence that began with their widely-criticised run defense stuffing Derrick Henry on fourth-and-goal at the one-yard line. Dak Prescott rewarded the turnover by igniting the following drive with a 49-yard strike to CeeDee Lamb, before KaVontae Turpin finished off the possession with a nine-yard touchdown run for a 28-24 lead with 9.42 to play.

After the teams exchanged punts Jackson orchestrated an 11-play 64-yard march culminating in his two-yard touchdown pass to Matthew Hibner with 1.30 left, prompting a steely pursed-lip look of determination from Prescott, enough to suggest this wasn't over. And it wasn't.

But instead of six, the Cowboys settled for three on the next possession as four plays inside the Ravens 10-yard line camp up empty, bringing out Aubrey for the field goal most believed had teed up overtime. Between Lamar and Loop, how wrong 'most' were.

Sunday's matchup marked the third to be played in Brazil following regular-season games at Corinthians Arena in Sao Paulo over the last two years. Rio meanwhile represented one of three new host cities alongside Melbourne, Australia and Paris, France this season as the NFL shows no signs of slowing in its international aspirations. It would have its sceptics, as international games tend to, but Rio and the league will wake up Monday morning having combined to produce one of football's most dramatic globe-trotting moments.

Next week, it is the turn of London once more as the UK welcomes three more games across October. Beat that.

The Cincinnati Bengals defense isn't good enough, yet. The first two weeks of the season displayed encouraging signs that Cincinnati might have finally mended the defense that has harmed their Super Bowl aspirations in recent seasons, Dexter Lawrence in particular appearing to add a new dimension to the interior of their defensive line. That narrative took a hit on Sunday as they suffered a 30-27 defeat to the Pittsburgh Steelers and Aaron Rodgers' much-maligned offense. Steelers running back Jaylen Warren in particular forced 10 missed tackles on the way to a career-high 176 yards from scrimmage, including 69 of 127 rushing yards before contact. That doesn't equate to a Championship-calibre team, no matter how incredible a trio of Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins is.

"Cook, he gets angry, and Cook starts cooking, the food was pretty good," Buffalo Bills offensive tackle Dion Dawkins told Sky Sports. He was referring to Bills running back James Cook, who had just underlined why he is perhaps still the most underrated and underappreciated player in the NFL by starring for Buffalo in their 24-16 win over the Chargers. Cook has been a defining piece to Joe Brady's offense ever since his early days as the Bills coordinator, his increased prominence proving the key difference from the Bills attack under Ken Dorsey. On a day when Josh Allen was far from his cleanest and most dominant, it was Cook who punished Chargers mistakes with 24 carries for 154 yards and a touchdown. Greg Rousseau meanwhile resumed his emphatic start to the season by recording two sacks for the third successive game, retaining his place as the league leader in that department. Between them came some further evidence of the Bills having ways to win beyond the heroics of their star quarterback.

The flip side to Buffalo's win was another edition of the Chargers finding new ways to hurt themselves, Jim Harbaugh's side wasting five turnovers in another dismal day for Mike McDaniel and Justin Herbert's offense. For a time their defense had Allen and Joe Brady's offense under wraps, but saw three first-half takeaways become just 10 points before a late collapse opened the door for Buffalo to take control. One of the staple moments came on Herbert's dreadful interception to CJ Gardner-Johnson, an ill-advised decision to, as Tom Brady lamented, "throw him a meatball sub" over the middle of the field negating back-to-back sacks including a fumble recovery. In very Chargers fashion they would then give up an automatic first down with the Bills staring at a second-and-26, paving the way for Allen's one-yard touchdown for a 17-13 lead with seven minutes to play. To make matters worse, Quentin Johnston reverted to serial dropper tendencies as he mis-held a Herbert bullet on third-and-10 on the next drive before the Chargers turned it over on downs.

Brock Purdy is the early - very very early - MVP frontrunner. The 49ers quarterback continued his near-faultless start to the season by throwing for 297 yards and four more touchdowns in San Francisco's 36-30 win over the Arizona Cardinals, two of his scoring strikes finding the hands of George Kittle. There is an argument he is playing the best football of any quarterback in football, his confidence epitomised by his touch-perfect touchdown pass to Mike Evans. He is clean, clinical and navigating an unbeaten team rediscovering some of its pizzazz on offense under Kyle Shanahan; as much tends to happen when the injury bug stays away, which still isn't quite the case after Evans and Trent Williams both picked up issues.

Mason Graham: The departure of Myles Garrett has opened the door for a fresh face at centre stage for the Cleveland Browns defense - step forward, Mason Graham. The second-year defensive tackle came up with two more sacks in Cleveland's 21-18 win over the Carolina Panthers, including a crucial stop on third-and-10 with the Panthers driving with 1.34 to play. In doing so he lifted his tally to four sacks through three games this season, his impact also underlining the pocket-squeezing influence of Jared Verse since arriving as part of the Garrett trade.

Patrick Mahomes: The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback underlined his place in greatness as he tied seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady for the most wins (115) by a quarterback in his first 150 career starts, including the playoffs. He looks as close to a prime Mahomes as the NFL has seen in at least two years, among his highlights in Kansas City's 24-10 win over Miami being a beautifully-timed strike to Noah Gray. The return to a heavy play-action scheme, boosted by the presence of Kenneth Walker III, has reignited both Mahomes and his passing attack. His Chiefs are now 3-0 and looking like contenders once more.

Mike Vrabel: The New England Patriots are in the middle of a miserable Super Bowl hangover. What was a championship-calibre defense is being torn apart and what was an MVP-contending quarterback in Drake Maye is struggling to maintain the heights of last season. Maye threw two more interceptions and lost a fumble to increase his turnover tally to seven in three games, having surrendered 11 in 17 regular-season games last season.

Brian Daboll/Cam Ward: Cam Ward threw his first interception in 209 pass attempts on Sunday, which would have been a forgivable blemish had it not been an end zone pick with 24 seconds left in the game. Jevon Holland would be the man to come up with a gift-wrapped throw by Ward as the New York Giants held on for a 12-7 victory, at which point cameras would quickly turn to Titans offensive coordinator and former Giants head coach Brian Daboll. Ward isn't Tennessee's only problem, but he is a problem and is struggling to look like a starting NFL quarterback.

Player of the Weekend - Jahmyr Gibbs, RB, Detroit Lions

Nothing typified Jahmyr Gibbs better than his shake-and-bake third-quarter touchdown run on Sunday, the Detroit Lions running back scurrying right before putting one defender on skates with a shimmy move to explode in the opposite direction on his way to the end zone. It was one of the latest reminders that he remains the heartbeat of Dan Campbell's Lions offense, contributing to three total touchdowns and 164 yards from scrimmage as Detroit held off a New York Jets fightback in a 31-24 victory. Only Jim Brown and Marshall Faulk have recorded more games with at least two rushing touchdowns and one receiving touchdown.

Sorry, the Ravens and Cowboys win the title of Game of the Weekend. Marcus Mariota delivered one of the surprise stories of the weekend as the backup veteran quarterback led the Washington Commanders to a 33-31 win over the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks while standing in for the injured Jayden Daniels. It would be Mariota who iced the game with a nine-yard scramble on third-and-seven to quash any Seahawks fightback. Sam Darnold returned for the Seattle for the first time since his injury early in the Week One win over the Patriots, but featured amid a mistake-ridden Seahawks performance that saw him intercepted on a crucial fourth-quarter pick-six by Kain Medrano. Mariota finished 19 of 31 for 183 yards and three touchdowns, seven of his passes going for over 10 yards as Washington clinched their first win of the season.

articles.title: NFL: Denver Broncos beat Los Angeles Rams and Seattle Seahawks lose
articles.summary: The NFL produced another thrilling day of action with a shock for the defending Super Bowl champions and several tight finishes.
articles.body:
The NFL produced another thrilling day of action on Sunday with a shock for the defending champions as five teams maintained their unbeaten record this season.

There were several nail-biting finishes as 12 of the 14 games were decided by eight points or fewer, tying the NFL record for the most one-score games in a day.

One of those took place in Brazil, where the NFL staged the second of a record nine international games to be played this season.

But they saved the best for last as the two teams that went within one win of last season's Super Bowl traded blows in a gripping primetime clash.

The Denver Broncos and the Los Angeles Rams remain potential Super Bowl contenders after losing last season's Conference Championship games.

Both teams had an underwhelming season opener before bouncing back last week, and Sunday's game in Denver gave them an opportunity to show their title credentials.

The Rams dominated the first half and led 16-0 at the interval, but the Broncos regrouped to draw level in the third quarter.

That set up a fascinating finish, with three lead changes in the final five minutes, beginning with an interception by Denver safety Talanoa Hufanga which he ran back for a 66-yard touchdown.

In just over a minute, last season's Most Valuable Player Matt Stafford led the Rams down the field, culminating in a 48-yard touchdown for receiver Konata Mumpfield to regain the lead.

The Broncos replied with quarterback Bo Nix reaching into the endzone after another long drive to put the hosts back in front.

That left Stafford 47 seconds to get into a game-winning position and he did just that. With two seconds left, he had a shot at the endzone from 19 yards, but Hufanga intercepted for a second time to clinch a 30-26 Broncos win.

The Washington Commanders' hopes of getting back in the play-offs were dealt a huge blow last week as quarterback Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow.

But Daniels could be back inside three weeks and, although the Commanders hosted defending champions the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, they led 24-10 after experienced back-up Marcus Mariota threw his third touchdown pass.

The Seahawks drew level in the fourth quarter, but Sam Darnold, who returned from a game out for Seattle, then threw his second interception, and it was returned by linebacker Kain Medrano for a 50-yard score.

That proved enough for Washington to clinch a 33-31 win and halt a 12-game win streak by Seattle, which included last season's Super Bowl run.

The New England Patriots were their opponents in the Super Bowl, but their quarterback Drake Maye has struggled since.

After having only 11 turnovers last year, he already has seven this season after another three against the Jacksonville Jaguars, and he was benched as the Jags romped to a 35-6 home win.

After playing in Sao Paulo the past two seasons, the NFL returned to Brazil for its first game in Rio de Janeiro.

There had been concerns about the condition of the field at the iconic Maracana stadium, but there were no issues.

The NFL picked a mouth-watering match-up for Rio and it delivered, with the Baltimore Ravens and the Dallas Cowboys producing a thriller.

Two Derrick Henry touchdowns helped the Ravens into a 24-13 lead in the third quarter before Dallas, playing only their second international game, fought back.

The lead changed hands twice in the fourth quarter and the game looked set for overtime when a Cowboys field goal levelled the score with seven seconds left.

But Lamar Jackson then completed a 27-yard pass down the middle to get the Ravens within field-goal range and Tyler Loop made a 56-yard kick as time expired to win the game 34-31.

That sparked wild celebrations at the Maracana and means all four AFC North teams have a 2-1 record this season.

Some Cleveland Browns fans cheered when quarterback Deshaun Watson suffered a season-ending injury in 2024.

Some booed as he returned to action in pre-season, but could Watson finally be winning over the 'Dawg Pound'?

The 31-year-old led the Browns to a comeback win at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last week and repeated the feat as Cleveland beat the Carolina Panthers 21-18 in their home opener.

Watson held his nerve to step out of the pocket and fire a 14-yard touchdown pass to tight end Harold Fannin Jr to cap a game-winning 65-yard drive.

"The past is the past," said Watson. "I know we've been through some ups and downs. But if we look forward, build off this win, come back Thursday night and get another big one, we can make something special for this city."

The Browns are at home again on Thursday against divisional rivals the Pittsburgh Steelers, who enjoyed a morale-boosting victory in another AFC North match-up on Sunday.

After only one offensive touchdown in their opening two games, Aaron Rodgers got the Steelers firing, throwing three touchdown passes before Derrick Harmon pulled off a strip-sack on Joe Burrow to seal a 30-27 win at home to the Cincinnati Bengals.

Three of the teams who remain unbeaten are regular play-off contenders. The Buffalo Bills came from 10-0 down to beat the Los Angeles Chargers 24-16, with quarterback Josh Allen barging over for two touchdowns.

Travis Kelce scored as the Kansas City Chiefs won 24-10 at the Miami Dolphins, while Brock Purdy threw four touchdown passes in the San Francisco 49ers' 36-30 win at home to the Arizona Cardinals.

Few expected the Minnesota Vikings to be 3-0, though. They won 23-16 at Tampa Bay despite losing receiver Justin Jefferson to an early ankle injury.

And the biggest surprise has been the Las Vegas Raiders. They have now won as many games as they did last season, when they had the league's worst record.

For the third straight game veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins threw for three touchdowns as the Raiders fought back from 27-16 down to win 35-27 at the New Orleans Saints.

The Philadelphia Eagles could make it six teams with a 3-0 record when they end week three with a trip to the Chicago Bears on Monday.

articles.title: Azeez Al-Shaair honours slain Palestinian sisters despite NFL sanctions
articles.summary: The Houston Texans linebacker wore eye black with the names of slain sisters Lana, 12, and Bana, eight.
articles.body:
American football player Azeez Al-Shaair has once again honoured Palestinian children killed by Israeli forces in Gaza, despite previous fines and the threat of being removed from games, this time wearing the names of sisters Lana and Bana Ahmad on his eye black during his latest National Football League (NFL) game.

The Houston Texans linebacker took the field against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday wearing the names of Lana, 12, and her sister Bana, eight, who were killed along with their family in an Israeli air attack earlier this month.

Hours before the game, Al-Shaair posted about the sisters on his Instagram account and followed it with a photo of the black tape bearing their names that he would later wear during the game. The image also showed part of Al-Shaair’s black shoes with flags of Palestine and Sudan stitched on them.

Al-Shaair, a Black American Muslim player, has repeatedly spoken about the plight of Palestinians. On September 13, he wore the name of Hind Rajab, the five-year-old girl who was killed in Gaza after Israeli soldiers opened fire on her family’s stranded car on January 29, 2024.

The NFL fined him $11,491 for breaching the league’s code of conduct on players’ clothing and equipment during a match against the Buffalo Bills.

However, basketball player Kyrie Irving stepped in and offered to pay the fine for Al-Shaair, who later confirmed that he had been in touch with the nine-time NBA All-Star.

Al-Shaair brushed off talk of the fine while speaking to reporters last week. “It’s bigger to me; what’s a life worth? Is a life worth $11,000? No, I think it’s priceless,” he said.

In his subsequent game against the Cincinnati Bengals, Al-Shaair then wore an eye black — a sticker or paint frequently used by NFL players to reduce glare — with the name of Wafa Akila, an eight-year-old who was killed along with her father in an Israeli attack in western Gaza as they were making their way home.

He was also fined in January, during the NFL’s last season, for displaying the message “Stop The Genocide” on his nose tape. While it did not specifically refer to a particular conflict, it was widely understood to be about Gaza and Sudan.

Following his NFL outing in which he wore the name of Rajab, Al-Shaair was informed he would have to remove the eye black or he would not be permitted to continue playing in the game, according to reports in US media.

US Democratic politician Isaiah Martin condemned the NFL’s reported reaction to Al-Shaair wearing eye black with the names of slain Palestinian children.

“This harms no one by letting him do this,” Martin said in a post on X. “I think it’s absurd they were fining him, but those were the ‘rules’ and he agreed to pay the fine. Removal from the game is INSANE. This shouldn’t stand!”

The Israeli genocide in Gaza has severely limited education for the Strip’s 660,000 children, with 90 percent of schools left damaged or destroyed.

Israel has killed at least 21,500 children since October 7, 2023, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health in Gaza.

articles.title: How Patrick Mahomes went from negotiating below the $475,000 ask on his first condo in 2017 to building a private compound from scratch just three years later
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes bought his first home in December 2017, a two-bedroom condo in Kansas City that reportedly sold for $350,000 against a $475,000 ask.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes bought his first home in December 2017, a two-bedroom condo in Kansas City that reportedly sold for $350,000 against a $475,000 ask. Three years later, in September 2020, he bought eight vacant acres in Belton, Missouri, and began planning a house from the ground up. His family moved into the finished compound in 2023. On paper the two purchases look like opposites, a modest city penthouse and a sprawling private estate. Together they show a quarterback who bought small, learned fast, then committed.How did Patrick Mahomes negotiate his first Kansas City condo?The unit sat in a 2004 building near Country Club Plaza. It covered about 1,800 square feet, with two bedrooms, three bathrooms, a two-car garage and a rooftop deck. Several outlets report he paid $350,000, well below the listed price.One caution on that number. The Kansas City Star cited Jackson County records showing $307,000, so the exact figure depends on the source. Either way, the discount was real, and it came soon after he signed with the Chiefs.A young player with new money could have overspent. Mahomes did not. He wanted a base near work, not a statement piece.The condo also had a short run as his main home. He listed it in 2019, found no buyer and pulled it from the market. It returned in July 2023 at $550,000, and Zillow showed it sold by October.How did Mahomes build a private compound so soon after?He moved in steps. In January 2019 he upgraded to a $1.8 million ranch-style house of roughly 4,300 square feet. Then came the land in Belton, listed at $400,000. Records do not show what he actually paid.Construction started in 2021, a pool followed in 2022, and the family settled in during 2023. The timeline matters here. The land deal happened just three years after the condo, but the house itself took nearly three more years to finish.The plan, it turns out, was older than the condo. Mahomes explained it in the Netflix docuseries Quarterback."I actually decided to get the land, to get ready to build that right when I signed my contract here in Kansas City," he said. "I knew I wanted to be here [in Kansas City]. So when I did that, I was like, 'I'mma be here, I might as well build the exact house I want.'"That changes how the condo reads. It was never the destination. It was a place to sleep while a bigger idea took shape. The 2019 ranch house served the same purpose, a comfortable middle step while the Belton plans came together.The location fits the goal too. Belton sits about half an hour from Arrowhead Stadium, close enough for game weeks but far enough to give a famous family some room. Reports describe a pool, a private pond and a small golf hole on the grounds. Those details come from media coverage rather than official listings, so treat them as reported.What stands out is the patience. Mahomes signed his big deal, then waited before spending on the dream. articles.title: Colts' Sauce Gardner relishes in first victory on US soil in more than 650 days
articles.summary: Sauce Gardner ended a 651-day winless streak on U.S. soil as the Indianapolis Colts edged the Houston Texans 19-17 in a dramatic Week 3 win.
articles.body: Indianapolis Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner was on the receiving end of a brutal graphic last week. The NBC broadcast noted that Gardner "has not won an NFL game in the United States since December 15, 2024," which at that point was 644 days. articles.body: Travis Kelce has put close to $2 million behind Operation Breakthrough, the Kansas City center that serves children living in poverty, according to the Chiefs. The total mixes his own donations with funds he directed to the group over the years. The team shared the number on January 7, after fans voted him winner of the Walter Payton Man of the Year Charity Challenge for a record third time. That win sends another $35,000 to a charity of his choice. But the foundation behind much of his giving is also facing questions about its finances.How much has Travis Kelce given to Kansas City kids?The Chiefs put the figure at nearly $2 million, all of it tied to Operation Breakthrough. That mix of personal gifts and directed funds matters. It is not one splashy check. It is years of steady money for a place that gives kids meals, classes and a safe room after school.The January win was fan voted, and Kelce became the first player to take the Charity Challenge three times. Kansas City missed the playoffs for the first time in a decade in 2025, so it was a rare bright spot for the franchise.His bigger investment came earlier. In 2020, Kelce bought a building for the Ignition Lab, a program for teenagers that opened in 2021. Students aged 14 to 18 pick up skills like graphic design, auto repair and cooking. Kelce has said it felt unsettling to learn the group's programs stopped at eighth grade. He called it "one of the coolest places that I've ever seen or been a part of."The foundation, Eighty-Seven & Running, began in 2015. In 2024 it also gave two $50,000 gifts to a GoFundMe for the Reyes family, whose two young daughters were hurt in the shooting at the Chiefs' Super Bowl parade.Will Travis Kelce's charity work last beyond his NFL career?That depends partly on how the foundation handles the scrutiny it now faces. CharityWatch reviewed its tax filings, along with reporting from The Arizona Republic. The foundation raised about $1.5 million and spent roughly $1.1 million over several years. About 41 cents of each dollar went to charitable programs, according to that review. A big share was booked as management and general costs, including fees paid to A&A Management Group, a firm linked to Kelce's longtime business managers.None of that erases the nearly $2 million that reached Operation Breakthrough. It does hand donors a fair question, though. Who checks where the money goes? Kelce has pointed fans to the foundation's website, and he has called giving back to Kansas City and his hometown "a dream come true."The setup gives the work a fair shot at outlasting his playing days. The Ignition Lab has a building, a partner organization and a steady flow of teenagers. Those pieces stay put when Kelce retires. What would help most is plainer reporting on how each dollar is used. articles.title: In 1997, Warrick Dunn used his rookie NFL season to help single parents buy homes after his own mother never got to fulfil that dream; 29 years later, his charity has furnished 252 homes and helped 687 people move into them
articles.summary: For Warrick Dunn, becoming an NFL player was never only about football.
articles.body: For Warrick Dunn, becoming an NFL player was never only about football. In 1997, during his rookie season with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, he turned a painful family memory into a mission that would last for decades. His mother, Betty Smothers, had dreamed of owning a home but died before she could see that dream come true. Nearly three decades later, Dunn's Homes for the Holidays programme has furnished 252 homes and helped 687 people move into them.Warrick Dunn turned his mother’s dream into a missionDunn was only 18 when his mother was killed in 1993. Smothers was a single mother raising six children while working as a police officer in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. Her death left the family facing an enormous loss, but it also left Dunn with a lasting understanding of what his mother had wanted for her children.She had dreamed of giving her family a home where they could have their own rooms, make memories and grow up with a sense of stability. After her death, Dunn used her life insurance to help the family purchase a home, turning part of her dream into reality.That experience stayed with him when he entered the NFL.The Tampa Bay Buccaneers selected Dunn with the 12th overall pick in the 1997 NFL Draft. During his first season, coach Tony Dungy encouraged players to become more involved in their communities. Dunn took that message personally. Instead of waiting until his career was established, he decided to act immediately.Dunn launched Homes for the Holidays in Tampa that year. The first effort helped three families move into their first homes around Thanksgiving. The moment changed the way he viewed his own success.“When I saw their reactions, it’s like, Wow, man, I just changed somebody’s life,” Dunn said. “I was like, I want to do this again.”He did exactly that.Homes for the Holidays gives single parents more than a houseThe programme's purpose has always gone beyond handing over keys. Warrick Dunn Charities works with local affordable housing providers to identify single-parent families who are purchasing their first homes.The charity does not provide the house itself. Instead, it helps turn that house into a home.Families can receive down-payment assistance, while volunteers furnish and decorate the property. That can include beds, furniture, kitchen supplies, food and even practical items such as lawn equipment and toothbrushes. The goal is to remove some of the financial pressure that comes with starting a new chapter.That distinction matters. A first home can bring a sense of security, but moving into an empty property can still create another financial burden. Dunn's programme addresses that gap.The charity describes its approach as a “hand-up” rather than a handout. Families must be actively working to support themselves, and the programme works alongside community partners to help them achieve greater stability.The idea also reflects what Dunn learned from his own childhood. His family received support from the Baton Rouge community after his mother's death. Dunn has spoken about how that generosity shaped his belief that people should help their neighbours when they have the opportunity.Warrick Dunn’s charity has now furnished 252 homesWhat began with three families in 1997 has grown into a nationwide effort.Warrick Dunn Charities currently lists 252 homes furnished and 687 people in homes, with more than $5 million in donations supporting its work. The organisation says Homes for the Holidays has operated across dozens of markets and continues to focus on single-parent families.The programme reached another major milestone in 2025 when Warrick Dunn Charities celebrated its 250th Homes for the Holidays recipient. The organisation also marked the programme's 28th anniversary that year.Its current impact figures show how far the original idea has travelled. The charity also reports more than $1.26 million in down-payment assistance and says 95% of its families remain in their homes.Those numbers offer a different way to measure Dunn's legacy. His NFL career lasted 12 seasons, included three Pro Bowl selections and earned him the 1997 AP Offensive Rookie of the Year award. Yet the work that began during that rookie season has continued long after his playing days ended.Warrick Dunn’s NFL legacy reaches far beyond footballThe impact of stable housing can extend beyond the parent who receives assistance. Dunn has said that helping parents also creates opportunities for their children to grow up in a more secure environment.Sports Illustrated previously reported that hundreds of children had benefited from the programme and highlighted research commissioned by Dunn's organisation suggesting that children in stable homes can experience improvements in school attendance, academic performance and participation in activities.One of those children was Deshaun Watson. Dunn's organisation helped Watson's family by furnishing their home after they had worked with Habitat for Humanity. Watson later became a Clemson star and eventually entered the NFL.Dunn's charitable work has also expanded beyond housing. Warrick Dunn Charities now supports programmes focused on education, financial empowerment, health and wellness, and community support.But Homes for the Holidays remains the heart of the story.Dunn entered the NFL carrying the memory of a mother who worked tirelessly to provide for her children. During his first season as a professional football player, he could have focused solely on establishing himself in the league. Instead, he used his new platform to help other families experience something his mother had wanted for her own.Twenty-nine years later, the numbers have grown far beyond those first three homes. But the idea remains remarkably simple: give a family a place to build memories, and give parents a chance to create the future their children deserve.That is the part of Warrick Dunn's NFL story that never needed a scoreboard.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Sunday's most compelling game was over and now it was time for the Denver Broncos stars to discuss their stirring victory over the Dallas Cowboys on NBC's national broadcast. And that's when quarterback Bo Nix and safety Talanoa Hufanga told everyone where the credit goes: To God. "Honestly man, all praise to God, just to come out here, believe in myself, believe in my teammates to be in the right spot," Hufanga said after collecting two interceptions, including a Pick Six. CARDINALS BACKUP CORNERBACK FINED BY NFL FOR WRITING 'GLORY BE 2 GOD' ON HIS EYEBLACK NBC's Melissa Stark turned to Nix and asked something about what was discussed at halftime. And the quarterback gave her 10 seconds of fluff football talk then said this: "But like he said, all glory to God," Nix said. "He's really good. He's given us this platform. He's given us this opportunity and our job is just to make the most of it." "Believe," Hufanga then added, as if imploring the audience to join them. And this is example 1,403,285 (more or less) that the NFL is the most God-centered professional sports league in America. CLEVELAND BROWNS PLAYERS PUBLICLY BAPTIZED AT CLEVELAND FOR CHRIST EVENT IN POWERFUL DISPLAY OF FAITH Every game day the most popular league playing the country's most popular sport shows up publicly thanking, praising and worshiping God. Unapologetically. No shame. No embarrassment. Out in the open, regardless how fans, media, or the league itself may feel about people of faith. So, how could this secular, oftentimes super liberal monolith of a business preach God so often? Well, let's understand there is a difference between the mostly faceless, nameless, Godless league that is headquartered in New York, and the people that fans actually come to see and cheer — the players and coaches. THE JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS OPENED TRAINING CAMP WITH AN AMAZING MESSAGE ABOUT GOD ON THEIR SOCIAL MEDIA While we think of the NFL as a sterile office bent on making gobs of profit, you've got people in uniform or wearing headsets that sometimes speak like prophets. Consider: The Baltimore Ravens beat the Dallas Cowboys in stunning, last-second fashion in Brazil. Quarterback Lamar Jackson completed a long pass with one second remaining to set up a final kick. So he stepped off the field and went to work. "The crazy thing about it [was] I had no doubt in my mind," Jackson told an international group of reporters afterward. "I prayed to Jesus. I prayed to God. "I am like, ‘Man, I feel like we already won.’ I could not show it, but I am like, I have all my faith in [kicker Tyler Loop] right now, man." In Washington, the Commanders lost linebacker Leo Chenal to a neck injury in the first half. He was taken to a local hospital where doctors saw he had movement in all his extremities. Back at the Northwest Stadium, Kain Medrano stepped in for Chenal. Medrano intercepted a pass in the fourth-quarter. And returned it for a touchdown and the game-deciding points. And afterward was thinking about his fallen teammate. "Yeah, obviously, we lost a brother," Medrano said, "but we're all praying for him." The Giants, like the Commanders, won on Sunday despite not having their starting quarterback because both Jaylen Daniels and Jaxson Dart are out injured. That put Jameis Winston at the reins of the New York offense, but it was the defense and safety Jevon Holland's interception at his own 4-yard line with 24 seconds to play that sealed the victory. And what was Winston's reaction? "Elated, praise God, so happy and grateful that he did what I thought he was going to do," Winston said. "I told [Holland] he was going to do that. He did it. "I told him he was going to do that Friday. Friday, I told him, I said, 'When the game is on the line, you're going to make the biggest play.'" Coach John Harbaugh's team has a 2-1 record now. Those two victories are already half the number of wins the Giants managed all of last season. So what's the first thing Harbaugh told the New York media to start his post-game news conference? "Praise and glory to our Savior," he said. "And to our guys, nothing but respect for finding a way to win a tough game in the fourth quarter. That's the way these games go usually in the National Football League." ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! None of this is preachy. It's not sanctimonious nor moralizing. It is people of faith feeling no shame about sharing what's in their heart. And at their core. This is the NFL on any given week. Despite an epic comeback win over the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football, Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton isn't pleased with how his team has performed three games into the 2026 season.

Payton said after Denver's 30-26 victory that he doesn't want comeback wins to become a habit for the Broncos, who improved to 2-1.

"I'm pleased with how we responded," Payton said, per ESPN's Jeff Legwold . "But we can't, like -- that'll cost us in bigger games. … It will be something we're frustrated about later if we can't clean it up.

"I'm comfortable with the grit of a team that can play well in the fourth quarter,'' he continued. "I'm uncomfortable with how we play at the start of games. … You're going to be in tight games, but as the head coach, you can't possibly be comfortable with the way the first half unfolded."

articles.title: Case Keenum reportedly expected to start for Bears with Caleb Williams out and Tyson Bagent recovering from concussion
articles.summary: Case Keenum hasn't started an NFL game since 2023.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears enter Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season already desperate for a win. After a standout showing in Week 1, the team's momentum was completely halted in Week 2, when it scored just three points and lost quarterback Caleb Williams to a hamstring injury in a loss to the Minnesota Vikings .

With Williams sidelined for Monday's contest against the Philadelphia Eagles , all eyes were initially turned to backup Tyson Bagent , who came on in relief of Williams in Week 2, but couldn't complete the comeback.

Instead, it will be veteran Case Keenum who gets the start for the Bears on "Monday Night Football," per NFL Network.

While Bagent was the logical choice to step into the starting role after Williams' injury, the backup was dealing with a concussion that kept him from practicing early in the week. Bagent cleared the NFL's concussion protocol Saturday and was able to get in a full practice, opening the door for him to potentially draw the start against the Eagles.

But the Bears will instead rely on Keenum, who practiced and prepared all week to be the team's starter.

It will mark Keenum's first NFL start since the end of the 2023 season, when he received two late-season starts with the Houston Texans . He went 1-1 in those two games, tossing a touchdown against three interceptions.

Keenum remained with the Texans in 2024, but did not play for the team after sustaining a season-ending injury before the start of the regular season.

After hitting the free-agent market after that year, Keenum signed with the Bears to be a veteran backup and mentor for both Williams and Bagent. The veteran has rarely been active for game days, often serving as the No. 3 option on the depth chart.

That will change Monday, as Keenum will draw his first start in years against a tough Eagles defense. If he can play a mistake-free game, and pick up a win, Keenum could force the Bears to consider him over Bagent in Week 4 if Williams is still sidelined by his hamstring injury for that contest.

articles.title: Tyler Shough Drops Honest Quote on NFL Rule After Saints' Controversial Loss to Cousins, Raiders
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints are searching for answers after another controversial fumble call cost them a win.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints are searching for answers after another controversial fumble call cost them a win.

In the fourth quarter of Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, Saints quarterback Tyler Shough lost the ball in the red zone, and it was recovered by Raiders star defensive end Maxx Crosby. While Shough appeared to have begun his throwing motion when he was hit in the arm, the call stood as a fumble. It was the first of four straight turnovers by the Saints in the final frame.

The situation conjured up memories of New Orleans' Week 1 loss to the Detroit Lions, in which a fumble by Jared Goff that was recovered and returned for a touchdown was overturned and ruled an incomplete pass. After Sunday's loss that dropped the Saints to 1-2 this year, Shough admitted that he's unclear about the league rules regarding the matter because he felt he should've been given the same ruling that Goff received.

Preseason Contenders in Desperation Mode 🗣️

"I thought I threw it. Me, personally, I thought my arm was going forward," Shough said, per ESPN's Katherine Terrell . "I'm not exactly sure on the rule. It doesn't really matter to me. I've got to get it out sooner regardless."

Terrell noted that Goff's fumble was ruled an incomplete pass "because of a little-known rule that states any intentional movement of the quarterback's hand starts a forward pass, even if the ball goes backward." Mark Butterworth, the NFL's vice president of instant replay, said in a pool report that he stood by the ruling on Shough's fumble because the defender hit both the ball and Shough's hand.

"The quarterback clearly lost control of the ball before his hand was coming forward," Butterworth said.

When asked about the similarities between Shough's fumble and Goff's incomplete pass, Butterworth said, "If the defender contacts the passer prior to the passer starting his throwing motion, it can be ruled as a backward pass. Because Goff had already started his throwing motion, and then the defender contacted him, it is therefore a forward pass."

The Saints have no choice but to regroup and try to bounce back when they face the NFC South rival Atlanta Falcons (1-2) on Monday Night Football in Week 4.

articles.title: The dozen games that turned Week 3 into one of the wildest in NFL history
articles.summary: Two seconds remained in regulation in Denver.
articles.body: Two seconds remained in regulation in Denver. One final play to decide the game. Could one of the wildest Sundays in NFL history have ended any other way? When Denver safety Talanoa Hufanga intercepted Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford in the end zone as time expired to seal a 30-26 comeback win on “Sunday Night Football,” it also capped a day that will be remembered for producing one thriller after another. Call it the Sunday of slim margins. Of the day’s 14-game slate in Week 3, 12 finished as one-score games, the most on any Sunday in NFL history. Thirteen games were within 8 points during the fourth quarter. Six teams won after go-ahead scores within the final three minutes. “It’s tough,” Rams coach Sean McVay said. “But this is sports.” After watching two weeks of offensive struggles under Denver’s new play caller, Broncos fans booed their team as they ran off the field after trailing the Rams, 16-0, at halftime. Then Denver scored 16 unanswered points, setting up a fourth quarter where the teams traded momentum swings. Hufanga intercepted Stafford and ran it back for a touchdown to lead, 23-19. When a Broncos defensive back fell down on the next possession, Stafford found an open receiver for an easy, go-ahead touchdown to lead, 26-23. Denver came back and moved the ball down the field after a succession of penalties, eventually taking a 30-26 lead and leaving the preseason Super Bowl favorite Rams only 47 seconds with which to try their own rally. It fell short by only a few yards, with no time left to spare — and it might not have even been Sunday’s wildest finish. In Rio de Janeiro, Baltimore got the ball back with seven seconds to play in regulation after Dallas had tied the score. Somehow, that was enough time for the Ravens to launch perhaps the latest comeback drive ever — at least since one database began tracking such figures — ending in Baltimore’s walk-off field goal from 56 yards. It was the first game since the 1970 merger to feature two teams that each made a field goal in the final 10 seconds. Improbable? It wasn’t the only game that fit the description. Previously winless, Washington couldn’t run the ball or convert third downs against Seattle yet knocked off the defending Super Bowl champion anyway, behind backup quarterback Marcus Mariota’s three touchdowns and three Seahawks turnovers. It ended the Seahawks’ 12-game winning streak and temporarily halted their historic run as the NFL’s best road team. In New Orleans, the Las Vegas Raiders improved to 3-0 after a 35-27 victory that saw the franchise match last season’s entire win total. They are now only the seventh team since the 1970 merger to open 3-0 after finishing the previous season with the league’s worst record, according to NBC Sports research. The Raiders pulled it off after trailing by 11 points in the second half. A controversial fumble call on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough helped the Raiders set up their go-ahead touchdown, but it was just one of four consecutive Saints turnovers forced by the Raiders in the second half. “In those big moments, there’s no panic,” Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby said. “We went down 11 and got together on the sideline and talked about not panicking.” Neither did the Bills (3-0). Like Baltimore and Las Vegas, Buffalo overcame a deficit of at least 10 points, eventually beating the Los Angeles Chargers, 24-16. It was the first time since 1997 that the Bills won a game despite committing at least five turnovers. Bills quarterback Josh Allen hadn’t committed a single turnover through two weeks, only to be intercepted twice and lose a fumble against Los Angeles (0-3). If Allen’s poor play was unexpected considering how good he had looked in MVP-level performances to begin the season, then what happened in Cleveland was the opposite. After ranking among the least efficient quarterbacks in the league for much of his tenure in Cleveland, Deshaun Watson has suddenly looked competent — and the Browns are now 2-1, after a 21-18 win. Watson threw two touchdowns, including a go-ahead score with 1:48 left in the fourth quarter. An interception of Carolina’s Bryce Young with seconds remaining clinched Watson’s 10th fourth-quarter comeback. Indianapolis (1-2) earned its first win since last November after Spencer Shrader kicked a 43-yard field goal with 16 seconds left for a 19-17 victory that dumps Houston, a preseason Super Bowl candidate, to 0-3. The Texans made the playoffs last year after starting 0-3, too, becoming only the seventh team in NFL history to do so. Another hard road to the playoffs awaits. In whipping rain and wind in New Jersey, the New York Giants held on for a 12-7 win in their first game since quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury. Sack artist Brian Burns injured his knee in the fourth quarter, and with 24 seconds left in regulation, Tennessee moved within 7 yards of a go-ahead touchdown. Instead, the Giants (2-1) survived after Jevon Holland intercepted Titans quarterback Cam Ward. In Tampa Bay, the Buccaneers played in their franchise-record ninth consecutive one-score game, but Minnesota (3-0) held on, 23-16, after batting down a desperate Hail Mary heave as time expired. For Tampa, what was even more dispiriting than falling to 0-3 was that quarterback Baker Mayfield left with a dislocated thumb that puts his active league-high streak of 54 consecutive starts in jeopardy. When Cincinnati quarterback Joe Burrow fumbled late in the fourth quarter, Pittsburgh exhaled with a 30-27 win over a division rival. It also breathed a sigh of relief for a different reason. Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, the NFL’s oldest active player, was showing his age. He entered Sunday having gone seven consecutive starts without throwing multiple touchdown passes. He responded with touchdown passes to three different receivers and led Pittsburgh (2-1) on a game-winning drive that ended with a 33-yard field goal with 2:15 remaining. Burrow’s fumble occurred just before the Bengals (2-1) could reach field-goal range of their own. With one game remaining in Week 3, six teams remain undefeated after San Francisco edged out a 36-30 win over Arizona. Can the 49ers keep it up, though? A franchise known for suffering a rash of injuries got more bad news Sunday when receiver Mike Evans (ribs) and left tackle Trent Williams (stinger) left the game. That left the Broncos and Rams to play a vital primetime game — the two Super Bowl contenders each hoping to avoid a second loss within their first three weeks. A pair of controversial defensive pass interference penalties on Denver’s go-ahead drive in the final minute rankled the Rams after the game, but comebacks have become something of a Broncos specialty. Last season, the Broncos’ 12 comeback wins set an NFL record. Last week, Denver overcame a 10-point deficit to beat Jacksonville. Sunday’s latest rally was the 50th fourth-quarter comeback of coach Sean Payton’s career to move past Mike Tomlin for fourth-most in NFL history. It relied on the 20th touchdown of quarterback Bo Nix’s career when trailing by one score — the most in the league since 2025, when Nix entered the NFL — and resulted in Nix’s seventh career fourth-quarter comeback. “Just a couple plays short that we left out there,” Rams receiver Konata Mumpfield said. On a day of wild finishes and tight margins, it was a sentiment shared across the league.

articles.title: Sean McVay Drops Brutally Honest Quote About Rams' Loss to Sean Payton, Broncos in New Video
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay didn't get too down on himself following his team's 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos on Sunday night.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay didn't get too down on himself following his team's 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos on Sunday night.

The Rams threw away a 16-point halftime lead as they suffered their second defeat of the season. McVay called it "tough" but said the result is something he and his players can learn from.

Rather than with what he said, McVay may have let reporters and fans read between the lines based on how he handled the presser. He wasn't exactly generous with his time.

The coach didn't delve too much into the controversial pass interference penalty that aided Denver's comeback, either.

Late in the fourth quarter, Rams cornerback Josh Wallace was flagged for interference despite Broncos receiver Pat Bryant initiating the contact. What could've been an interception instead turned into a first down, and the Broncos took the lead later on the drive.

McVay told reporters his initial impression was that it "looked like it was a good, competitive play from my vantage point."

If Wallace's interception stands, Los Angeles likely holds on to win. But that stroke of bad luck isn't the sole reason the Rams lost.

Matthew Stafford threw a costly pick-six in the fourth quarter and had another interception on the game's final play as L.A. was inside the red zone.

The Rams battle another playoff contender in Week 4 as they hit the road to play the Philadelphia Eagles. There are some issues for McVay and his staff to iron out as they draw up their game plan.

articles.title: "We didn’t play to our standard”: Patrick Mahomes opens up on Chiefs’ performance despite impressive 3-0 start
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ star player and popular quarterback, has remained unbeatable on the field in the new season after recovering from
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ star player and popular quarterback, has remained unbeatable on the field in the new season after recovering from his severe injuries. The Kansas City Chiefs secured their third consecutive win in the new season after beating the Miami Dolphins but it seems the popular quarterback is not that happy.Patrick Mahomes expresses disappointment amid the Chiefs' win in Week 3A few hours ago, after the Kansas City Chiefs defeated the Miami Dolphins, Patrick Mahomes spoke to reporters about the game as he said, "I mean, at the end of the day, we won the football game, and we found a way to win and win by two touchdowns. Obviously, we didn't play to our standard that we would hold for ourselves, especially in that middle part offensively of the game, kind of second quarter through third quarter…It'll be a learning experience for us to know that we have to come with our A-game every single time to win. But at the end of the day, we're 3 -0."The three time Super Bowl Most Valuable Player added, "I wouldn't say I feel disappointed. I'm happy for the win. I think last year taught me that you can't be disappointed when you win football games. You have to enjoy every single one of them, enjoy the plane ride back, everything like that…”Patrick Mahomes continued, “But I know we can be better. I know we can get better, and that's going to take watching the tape and going out and having a better week of practice, communicating within the entire offense and the entire team. We're going to be happy. We're going to enjoy this victory, but we know to get better and better. That if we want to get to where we want to go, we have to continue. articles.title: Bengals News: Ja’Marr Chase reaches major NFL molestone
articles.summary: And he beat a coule of hall of famers doing it.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals have clearly found a great player in Ja'Marr Chase. He reached a milestone on Sunday that reminds us of that. He became the fourth quickest player in NFL history to reach 7,000 receiving yards .

Chase reached this milestone in 81 games. That beats out hall of famers Randy Moss and Jerry Rice who took 83 games to do it.

Beating those two isn't necessarily the main point. It just shows that Chase continues to be on path consistent with hall of fame receivers. It is obviously a long-term view of things, but it is nice to find a bright spot after such a tough loss.

There are certainly obvious areas to blame from this loss, but it takes a group effort to lose a game like that. Between the defensive struggles, special team blunders and the late turnover by Joe Burrow to effectively end the game, the blame can be passed however you see fit. It is certainly a humbling loss early in the season.

"Like last week with the penalties, we just can't shoot ourselves in the foot like that," Burrow said. "You can't win in this league when you do that. It's really hard. It's really hard. We could have overcome it, but it's hard to win like that."

Burrow and the team have some work to do before their next game. Better to have a soul searching loss in Week 3 though.

It is a little surprising to see the Bengals as favorites, even with it being at home. If the Jaguars learned anything from the Steeelers' offensive game plan then it could certainly be a long day at the office on Sunday.

Ekeler had a decent run with the team before injuries got in the way. Adding a veteran of his caliber to a group is never a bad thing. It will be interesting to see how much of a role he plays.

For those wondering why the Bengals almost certainly won't be looking to trade Joe Flacco ,these backup quarterbacks are playing more and more, and having someone as reliable as Flacco is a luxury.

After trading away Dexter Lawrence to the Bengals this offseason, Burns became that much more important rushing the passer. As always, such a terrible thing to see have happen to a player after working so hard for the season.

articles.title: Quarterback review: Lamar Jackson outduels Dak Prescott in Brazil
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson’s efficiency and late touchdown drive gave him the edge over Dak Prescott in Baltimore’s 34-31 victory
articles.body:
Lamar Jackson and Dak Prescott took different paths to the same late-game destination Sunday in Brazil. Both quarterbacks led critical fourth-quarter drives, but Jackson and the Ravens earned the final possession and the victory.

Jackson completed 15 of 20 passes for 186 yards and two touchdowns. He committed no turnovers or sacks, finishing with a 136.7 passer rating. His 50 rushing yards added another dimension and helped Baltimore finish with 192 yards on the ground.

His most important work came after Dallas erased an 11-point deficit. Trailing 28-24, Jackson directed an 11-play, 64-yard drive and connected with Hibner for a 21-yard touchdown.

Prescott was asked to carry more of the Cowboys' offense. He completed 25 of 40 attempts for 276 yards and one touchdown. Dallas trailed 24-13 before Prescott helped direct three consecutive scoring possessions. His final drive covered 60 yards in 1:23 and set up Aubrey's tying field goal. Prescott also reached 250 career passing touchdowns, joining Russell Wilson , Aaron Rodgers , John Elway and Fran Tarkenton as quarterbacks with 250 touchdown passes and 30 rushing scores.

Prescott produced more volume overall, but Jackson was more efficient. Baltimore's quarterback also delivered the touchdown drive that set up Loop's winning kick.
